trickyParts: The point of the separate hook bundle is the module graph, not the file list: an ESM entrypoint evaluates everything it imports before it reads argv, so a mode check could never have saved the cost. src/session-identity.ts imports zod for its role schema, which is why the title helpers had to move out of it rather than simply be imported from the new hook.

pruneStateDirectory's predicate takes the entry's full path and may be async, so the liveness rule reads the pid from the basename and the age rule stats the file. rm is recursive and forced, which covers both shapes the three directories hold (a sessions/<pid> directory, a titles/ or roles/ file).

Title files are titles/<id>.txt with no read of the old suffix-less name: a clean cutover. A machine whose installed bundle is older than the channel server, or the reverse, shows the fallback title until the next prompt after both sides are the new build, and the record is cosmetic and self-healing.
deviations: The architect's first instruction kept pruneStaleSessionHandoffs out of the shared sweep; its later one (01:49) converged with the reviewer's fast-follow and asked for one pruneStateDirectory with liveness and age as predicates. Built the later way, so nothing is left for a fast-follow.
SESSION_TITLE_MAX_AGE_MS is renamed STATE_FILE_MAX_AGE_MS, since the titles and the roles now share the thirty-day policy.

The whole browser suite was run in this pod for the chromium project only (721 rows, complete). The iphone project's remainder was cut by the command's own 58-minute cap and then re-run for the thirteen specs that touch this change (98 rows); the webkit, webkit-iphone, firefox and firefox-download-navigation projects cannot run here at all — Playwright's host validation names the missing system libraries (libgtk-4, the gstreamer set, libflite and the rest) and this container has no root. CI covers those four projects, and the one row of this change's concern that runs in them, keyboard-agents-picker.e2e.ts:835, is fixed by an engine-independent attribute selector.
openQuestions: The queryTmux bound row is honest now and still red about a third of full-suite runs in a Legion pod, and my earlier diagnosis — which I gave the architect and which the first round's handoff carried — was wrong. Item 7 made the child time its own queryTmux call, with Bun's start-up and the import excluded, and the failures persisted at 5018, 5019, 5023, 5025 and 5042 ms: the inner call really does run the stub's whole five-second sleep. The cause is the runtime, not the harness: a bare `Bun.spawnSync({cmd: ['sleep','5'], timeout: 1000, killSignal: 'SIGKILL'})` in this container returns 1004 ms/SIGKILL, 1003 ms/SIGKILL, 1004 ms/SIGKILL, 5006 ms/exit 0 — I reproduced that myself, Bun 1.3.14 on linux 4.19.0-gvisor. So execFileSync's timeout, which is the only thing bounding queryTmux, is delivered unreliably under gVisor, and on a host where the kill misses a hung tmux would hold the channel server's startup for as long as tmux hangs rather than one second. CI's ubuntu runners are green on the row. Making the bound real needs a design decision outside this round — queryTmux bounding itself, which means building a shell command string from the TMUX socket and pane and so a quoting surface argv-based execFile does not have today, or the pane lookup becoming async — and it is reported to the architect rather than decided here.
discoveredComplexity: The browser rig is reproducible in a pod and the tester left most of it on the issue volume: PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector unpacked under /legion/scratch/dispatch-e2e-rig/pg17 (its data directory must be the caller's own, in its container's /tmp), the Playwright browser cache at /legion/scratch/cache/ms-playwright, and a warm Go module cache at /legion/go/mod. A pod is roughly three times slower than CI at this suite: the chromium project alone took about 50 minutes here against CI's 42 for everything.

Three of the four Playwright projects CI runs cannot run in a worker pod at all, for want of system libraries no agent can install. Any future round that must prove a WebKit or Firefox behaviour locally needs that gap closed first.
